package_info.why_malicious: The report provides a high-level overview of several real-world software supply chain attacks (Jenkins exploitations, Verkada breach, Codecov incident, Log4Shell, and dependency confusion attacks) but does not specify a particular malicious package or provide concrete code snippets. Instead, it describes attack techniques and their impact on development infrastructure and supply chains.

execution_context.trigger: import-time/runtime (Log4Shell); build-time (dependency confusion); CI/CD runtime (Jenkins, Codecov)
execution_context.file_location: Log4j library (Log4Shell); public package repositories (dependency confusion); Jenkins build scripts; Docker containers (Codecov)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: No explicit code provided. Example behaviors include: remote code execution via crafted log messages (Log4Shell), malicious code in counterfeit packages (dependency confusion), unauthorized scripts in CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, Codecov).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Executes attacker-controlled code by exploiting vulnerabilities or by being included as a malicious dependency or build script. Can exfiltrate secrets, mine cryptocurrency, or provide remote access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Execution of code from untrusted sources, especially during build or runtime, is highly suspicious. Use of public repositories to inject malicious code or exploiting vulnerabilities for remote code execution is a hallmark of supply chain attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior expects only vetted, trusted code to execute in build and runtime environments. Malicious code violates this by executing attacker-controlled payloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated build scripts and dependency management are legitimate, but only when using trusted sources and without arbitrary code execution.
key_indicators: Execution of code from unexpected sources
Unexpected file or environment variable access
Use of public repositories for internal dependencies

attack_chain.action: Attacker introduces malicious code into the supply chain (via public repository, vulnerable library, or compromised build environment).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is incorporated into build or runtime environments.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes during build, deployment, or runtime, leveraging available permissions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Performs actions such as exfiltrating secrets, mining cryptocurrency, or enabling lateral movement.

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to sensitive data, internal systems, or customer environments.
attack_chain.leads_to: Broader compromise of organizational or customer assets.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network connections from build or runtime environments
Execution of code from newly introduced or unvetted dependencies
Modification of build scripts or CI/CD pipelines
Remote code execution triggered by crafted input (e.g., log messages)
file_indicators: Presence of unfamiliar or similarly named packages in dependency lists
Unexpected changes to build scripts (Jenkinsfiles, Dockerfiles, etc.)
Unusual files or binaries in build environments
network_indicators: Outbound connections to unrecognized domains or IPs during build or runtime
Connections to known attacker infrastructure (e.g., webhook.site, suspicious cloud endpoints)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for the introduction of new or unvetted dependencies, especially those with names similar to internal packages. Implement behavioral monitoring for unexpected network activity or file access during build and runtime. Use software composition analysis (SCA) tools to verify the integrity and provenance of all dependencies. Continuously audit build scripts and CI/CD configurations for unauthorized changes or suspicious commands. Detect remote code execution attempts by monitoring for unusual process launches or crafted input patterns (e.g., JNDI lookups in logs).
